claims.claim: A 1965 British official memo described a strategy to frighten Mauritius's premier with hope of independence unless he cooperated on detaching the Chagos Archipelago.
claims.verbatim: The object is to frighten him with hope: hope that he might get independence; Fright lest he might not unless he is sensible about the detachment of the Chagos Archipelago.
claims.source: Note prepared 22 September 1965; ICJ Advisory Opinion paragraph 105 — Sir Oliver Wright (Private Secretary to PM Harold Wilson)

claims.claim: British Prime Minister Wilson told Mauritius's premier in 1965 he could return home either with independence or without it.
claims.verbatim: The Premier and his colleagues could return to Mauritius either with Independence or without it.
claims.source: ICJ Advisory Opinion paragraph 107 — PM Wilson to Premier Ramgoolam, Lancaster House, 23 September 1965

claims.claim: The International Court of Justice found that the 1965 detachment of the Chagos Archipelago was not based on the free and genuine will of the people concerned.
claims.verbatim: this detachment was not based on the free and genuine expression of the will of the people concerned.

claims.claim: The International Court of Justice ruled 13-1 that the United Kingdom's continued administration of the Chagos Archipelago is an internationally wrongful act.
claims.verbatim: the United Kingdom's continued administration of the Chagos Archipelago constitutes a wrongful act entailing the international responsibility of that State.

claims.claim: In 1964 secret talks, US officials said the islands were wanted under exclusive control without local inhabitants present.
claims.verbatim: exclusive control (without local inhabitants)
claims.source: Island of Shame page 78; U.S. Embassy London telegram — Kitchen and Sloan (U.S. officials), secret talks 1964

claims.claim: A steamship company representative told Chagossian Rita Bancoult in Mauritius that her island had been sold and she would never return.
claims.verbatim: Your island has been sold. You will never go there again.

claims.claim: British agents and US troops on Diego Garcia herded the Chagossians' pet dogs into sealed sheds and gassed and burned them in front of their owners before deportation.
claims.verbatim: herded the Chagossians' pet dogs into sealed sheds and gassed and burned them in front of their traumatized owners awaiting deportation.
claims.source: Island of Shame page 1 — Marcel Moulinie under order of BIOT Commissioner Sir Bruce Greatbatch

claims.claim: Chagossian Rita Bancoult described her forced removal as being pulled from paradise and put into hell.
claims.verbatim: It's as if I was pulled from my paradise to put me in hell.

claims.claim: The 2025 UK-Mauritius treaty permits Chagossian resettlement on the Chagos Archipelago except on Diego Garcia.
claims.verbatim: Mauritius is free to implement a programme of resettlement on the islands of the Chagos Archipelago other than Diego Garcia.
claims.source: Agreement between UK and Mauritius, Article 6 (2025)

claims.claim: UN human rights experts said the 2025 UK-Mauritius agreement fails to guarantee the Chagossian right to return, effective remedy, reparations, and cultural rights.
claims.verbatim: fails to guarantee and protect the rights of the Chagossian people, including their right to return to Diego Garcia, effective remedy and reparations and their cultural rights.
claims.source: OHCHR Press Release, 10 June 2025 — Nicolas Levrat, K.P. Ashwini, Bernard Duhaime, Bina D'Costa

claims.claim: US military planners once described their strategic aim as being able to run the planet from Guam and Diego Garcia.
claims.verbatim: to run the planet from Guam and Diego Garcia

claims.claim: Diego Garcia has been described as the single most important military facility in the region, filling the power vacuum left by British withdrawal East of Suez.
claims.verbatim: The single most important military facility we've got

claims.claim: The UK argued at the ICJ that it held continuous sovereignty over the Chagos Archipelago since the 1814 Treaty of Paris.
claims.verbatim: Continuous sovereignty since 1814

claims.claim: The UK argued Chagos was linked to Mauritius only for administrative convenience, never actually forming part of Mauritius.
claims.verbatim: administrative convenience

claims.claim: The UK argued the Royal Prerogative permitted detaching Chagos from one colony to another as a matter of constitutional law.
claims.verbatim: Royal Prerogative allows detaching territory from one colony to another

claims.claim: The UK argued the Mauritian negotiating team was democratically elected and had sufficient mandate to consent to detachment.
claims.verbatim: democratically elected

claims.claim: The UK argued it had committed to return the Chagos Archipelago once it was no longer needed for defence purposes.
claims.verbatim: no longer needed for defence purposes

claims.claim: The UK argued the ICJ's advisory opinion was not legally binding and that the General Assembly's referral was a misuse of powers.
claims.verbatim: misuse of powers

claims.claim: Dissenting Judge Donoghue argued the ICJ should have declined to give an advisory opinion because the matter was fundamentally a bilateral sovereignty dispute.
claims.verbatim: quintessentially bilateral... dispute over territorial sovereignty

claims.claim: Judge Donoghue argued the General Assembly's request for an advisory opinion had the effect of circumventing the UK's absence of consent to judicial settlement.
claims.verbatim: has the effect of circumventing the absence of United Kingdom consent

claims.claim: The UK stated it fully accepts the Chagossians' removal and subsequent treatment was shameful and wrong, while denying legal culpability.
claims.verbatim: The UK fully accepts that the manner in which the Chagossians were removed... and the way they were treated thereafter, was shameful and wrong, and it deeply regrets that fact.

claims.claim: Mauritius received a payment of three million pounds as part of the 1965 deal that detached the Chagos Archipelago.
claims.verbatim: £3 million payment

claims.claim: Mauritius's Premier Ramgoolam told Parliament the country had no choice but to accept the 1965 detachment deal.
claims.verbatim: we had no choice

claims.claim: Chagossians resettled in Mauritius were left languishing on the beach while a promised resettlement grant went unimplemented.
claims.verbatim: languishing on the beach

claims.claim: 1980s surveys found a 58 percent unemployment rate among Chagossian women resettled in Mauritius.
claims.verbatim: 58% unemployment rate for Chagossian women (1980s surveys)

claims.claim: Mauritius agreed in the 2025 treaty to bar Chagossian resettlement on Diego Garcia for ninety-nine years.
claims.verbatim: bar Diego Garcia resettlement for 99 years

claims.claim: Critics say the 2025 treaty's resettlement clause is in substance declaratory and does not secure the Chagossian right to return.
claims.verbatim: in substance declaratory

claims.claim: The Chagos Refugees Group, led by Olivier Bancoult, called the 2025 deal a historic day, welcoming the completion of Mauritian decolonization.
claims.verbatim: historic day for us

claims.claim: Chagossian Voices sought recognition as an indigenous people before the UN while opposing the 2025 deal's denial of full return rights.
claims.verbatim: indigenous people

claims.claim: Judge Sebutinde argued Chagossians possess a distinct societal and cultural identity separating them from the wider Mauritian people.
claims.verbatim: societal/cultural identity that separates them from wider Mauritian people

claims.claim: The ICJ ruled Chagos detachment unlawful by applying a heightened-scrutiny consent standard to colonial agreements, not on grounds of generalized coercion.
claims.verbatim: heightened scrutiny

claims.claim: The ICJ held that conditioning Mauritius's independence on surrendering territory subverted the true will of the colonial people.
claims.verbatim: This subverted the true will of the colonial people

claims.claim: The ICJ treated decolonization as a multilateral obligation owed to the whole international community, requiring the UK to end unlawful administration regardless of Mauritius's consent.
claims.verbatim: Requires UK to cease unlawful administration regardless of Mauritius consent

claims.claim: The ICJ confirmed Mauritius's territorial integrity as a corollary of self-determination but left Chagossian resettlement modalities to the UN General Assembly.
claims.verbatim: relegated Chagossian resettlement to UN General Assembly for "modalities"

claims.claim: Unlike Chagos, the UK's Cyprus Sovereign Base Areas did not require deporting the local population when Cyprus gained independence.
claims.verbatim: strategic population cleansing

claims.claim: Unlike Chagos, Gibraltar's population determines the territory's future through their own right of self-determination.
claims.verbatim: Gibraltarian people determine territory's future via self-determination

claims.claim: Unlike Chagos, Mayotte's population voted in a referendum to remain with France when France separated it from the Comoros in 1975.
claims.verbatim: Mayotte voted to stay with France

claims.claim: The US secretly agreed with Denmark to remove about 150 Inughuit people from Thule, Greenland, part of a broader pattern of strategic island expulsions.
claims.verbatim: US secret agreement with Denmark to remove 150 Inughuit

claims.claim: Thousands of Marshall Islanders displaced from Kwajalein were relocated to a small island described as a ghetto of the Pacific.
claims.verbatim: ghetto of the Pacific

claims.claim: The UK has defied the UN General Assembly's withdrawal deadline and maintains it will only cede Chagos when no longer needed for defence.
claims.verbatim: UK defied UNGA deadline, maintains will only cede when "no longer needed for defence"

claims.claim: There is no guarantee the forty-million-pound Chagossian trust fund created by the 2025 treaty will be under Chagossian control.
claims.verbatim: no guarantee £40M fund will be Chagossian-controlled

claims.claim: The UK detached the Chagos Archipelago on 8 November 1965, three years before Mauritius's independence on 12 March 1968.
claims.verbatim: 8 November 1965

claims.claim: Between 1,500 and 2,000 Chagossians were deported from the islands between 1967 and 1973.
The 2025 UK-Mauritius treaty commits the UK to pay Mauritius roughly 3.4 billion pounds via 101 million pounds annually for ninety-nine years.
claims.verbatim: £101 million for 99 years

claims.claim: The UN General Assembly voted 116-6 demanding the UK withdraw from the Chagos Archipelago.
claims.verbatim: 116-6 (demanding UK withdrawal)

claims.claim: The 2025 treaty grants the UK a 99-year lease on Diego Garcia, extendable to 139 years.
claims.verbatim: 99 years, extendable to 139

claims.claim: The 1956 Suez Crisis raised US fears of a Cold War power vacuum in the Indian Ocean as Britain's long-term regional control was questioned.
claims.verbatim: power vacuum
claims.source: Causal Sequence (Cold War Anxiety to Strategic Island Concept)

claims.claim: Planners selected Chagos for the base partly because it was judged a neglected minor backwater with minimal population.
claims.verbatim: Neglected minor backwater

claims.claim: British officials maintained a policy of pretending the islands' inhabitants were not permanent residents to avoid triggering UN scrutiny of the base.
claims.verbatim: maintain the fiction that inhabitants are not permanent
